pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

This PR adds a new plugin that shows date and time in different formats.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/61519853/157034386-7c58b09c-1429-4021-a770-7317c2891611.png)

For the date and time format the plugin uses the culture settings in Windows, if the format is not commonly defined. The user can search for the system date/time or a custom date/time. The value of each result can be copied to clipboard.

**Available commands:**
- [x] Time: 05:50 am.
- [x] Now: 01/01/2022 05:50 am.
- [x] Date: 01/01/2022
- [x] Unix timestamp (now): 1646135767
- [x] Hour: 10
- [x] Minute: 30
- [x] Second: 45
- [x] Millisecond: 678
- [x] Day: Tuesday
- [x] Day of week: 4
- [x] Day of month: 20
- [x] Day of year: 350
- [x] Week of year: 15
- [x] Week of month: 2
- [x] Month: January
- [x] Month of year: 1
- [x] Month and day: March 7
- [x] Year: 2022
- [x] Era: AD
- [x] Era abbreviation: A
- [x] Year and month: March 2022
- [x] Windows file time as number
- [x]  YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss
- [x] ISO 8601
- [x] RFC1123

### Settings
Lable | Default value
------------- | -------------
Show only 'Time', 'Date', and 'Now' result on global queries | true
Show time with seconds (Applies to 'Time' and 'Now' result) | false
Show date with weekday and name of month (Applies to 'Date' and 'Now' result) | false
Hide 'Invalid number input' error message on global queries | false

## How does someone test / validate:
Tested the new plugin on a local build.

## Quality Checklist

- [x] **Linked issue:** #15950, #9544
- [x] **Communication:** I've discussed this with core contributors in the issue. 
- [x] **Tests:** Added/updated and all pass
- [x] **Analyzer:** Enabled/Warnings fixed (#16511)
- [x] **Installer:** Added/updated and all pass
- [x] **Localization:** All end user facing strings can be localized
- [x] **Docs:** Added/ updated
   - [x] Dev docs
   - [x] User docs => New issue: #16630
- [x] **Binaries:** Any new files are added to WXS / YML
   - [ ] No new binaries
   - [x] [YML for signing](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/.pipelines/pipeline.user.windows.yml#L68) for new binaries
   - [x] [WXS for installer](https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/main/installer/PowerToysSetup/Product.wxs) for new binaries

A CLA must be signed. If not, go over [here](https://cla.opensource.microsoft.com/microsoft/PowerToys) and sign the CLA.

It happens often enough, I'm actually tempted to try to figure out if I can add some intelligence to add a warning about it.

I strongly believe this should be functionality moved into the system plugin. More i think about this, we're adding an extra DLL and complexity for something that can be in the Setting plugin.  System doesn't have to be a "pure" 1:1 mapping.

This adds unneeded disk and RAM usage.  Also makes the build slower due to extra DLL that needs to be built + signing.

> I strongly believe this should be functionality moved into the system plugin. More i think about this, we're adding an extra DLL and complexity for something that can be in the Setting plugin.  System doesn't have to be a "pure" 1:1 mapping.
> 
> This adds unneeded disk and RAM usage.  Also makes the build slower due to extra DLL that needs to be built + signing.

I personally don't agree. The code for the new feature is completely different from the one of the system plugin. Combining them would bring extra complexity in code and new problems I think. We than have to check if it's a system command or a date/time result  and act differently. (Especially because of the custom date/time converting feature.)

(Btw. because of the needed multiple search tag feature we have to rewrite search logik in a more complex way.)

> @jaimecbernardo There is a bug that when searching for `date` the "Era" results aren't shown. But only when searching in PT Run. The unit tests working as expected and get the correct results. Can you take a look. After hours I still have no idea whats going wrong.
> 
> xref: #16783

@htcfreek, it looks like for the UI it's inside the SearchController.cs. The Fuzzy Search for the alternativeMatch gives success but the Score is 0, which is weird. I think it's a function of matching something closer to the end of the string, which has less value. I think the code around the FuzzySearch in SearchController.cs for the TimeDate plugin is where you'll have to do some tweaks to make it work.

But what is the default score. If I don't set it (show all results) it's shown. Reworking the matching code is planned because we need multiple tags per result.
The score for date is 0. The score for "da" seems to work because it's matched twice (in "calendar" and "date")

> The score for date is 0. The score for "da" seems to work because it's matched twice (in "calendar" and "date")

Aaargh. That's the match I didn't understand: "da" matches "calendar". 😅

But what I mean is when you only type the activation key for the plugin, no score ist set. Does PT Run shows only results with score 0 if no result has a score >0?

Basically Date is not good because it's to the end and doesn't match much of the string it's comparing against.
You might want to do a pre-pass there in Microsoft.PowerToys.Run.Plugin.TimeDate.ComponentsSearchController, get the AlternativeSearchTag, divide it into the words you expect to match and do the fuzzy search against each of them. This should allow you to get better results.

@jaimecbernardo 
I found the reason: "If the `GregorianCalendar` is selected in `DateTimeFormatInfo.Calendar`, `DateTimeFormatInfo` ignores punctuation in abbreviated era names; that is, 'A.D.' is equivalent to 'AD'."

The plugin code is ready for review. All bugs (tests, culture/format and search) are fixed.

@jaimecbernardo
I couldn't find the reason why the tests are failing with fixed expected values for the "Era" results. I have fixed the tests by now calculating the expected era results at runtime.

@crutkas
I think this feature can't be an addition to system plugin. I have the following reasons for my opinion:
- The plugin has to many features to be a small addition for system plugin.
- The code is different to the one from system plugin and much more complex. Implementing this features into system plugin requires a nearly complete rewrite of the system plugin code.
- This plugin cost me a week of hard work. Implementing this into the system plugin would mean that my name isn't mentioned as author. And this is something I don't agree.

This doesn't look like something to include in the system plugin.
- System plugin runs system commands like log off, shutdown, etc.
- TimeDate plugin shows time values, manipulating them and allows you to extract things like week number from dates that are not even the system date and you introduce as an input.

I don't think the use cases / users would overlap all that much to make these the same plugin.

@jaimecbernardo
Implementing the whole word match requirement for global searches makes user experience in some cases very bad. I think the problem here is the scoring of the other plugins. I simply use fuzzy search and I would expect that all plugins behave in the same way. What should we do here?

An idea would be to match on global queries only for queries with at least two chars or an calculated min. number of chars.

But I have changed how scores are adjusted. Can you test it and give me some feedback.

@jaimecbernardo
The feedback is implemented. 
I added some requirements for global queries:
- If the query is a word of the following conjunction list, we don't return any results: for, and, nor, but, or, so
   - We don't have 'yet' (synonym of 'now') on the list, because this could block results in some languages.
- The first word of the query has to be a full match with a word in the label or tag list. 
- For both requirements we compare case-insensitive.

Can you please test, if the behavior now fits the user experience you like to have?

You can still review. I only missed to add the settings note and to update the tests

issue_context.title: Enable analyzers for each project
issue_context.body:
Enable analyzer by setting
```xml
<EnableNETAnalyzers>true</EnableNETAnalyzers>
<AnalysisMode>Recommended</AnalysisMode>
```
in each csproj file and fix all upcoming warnings.

> I think we should slowly roll it up and get stuff up. Small single targeted scope and when ready, we do the actual flip. 
>
> It is how we got all the other stuff up with the old analyzers. Turn it on, fix one code or two so it is still reviewable, then turn it off and do the PR
>
> this is a slow burn adjustment. 
>
> This is same concept we are doing for arm 64. Slowly swapping / transition needed parts

_Originally posted by @crutkas in https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/8463#issuecomment-1046057132_
comments: do we have a list which currently don't have this enabled?

I needed to touch about 50 files to fix all warnings. Most of them with very minor changes (One line changes).
